source.title: Robust LLM Unlearning with MUDMAN: Meta-Unlearning with Disruption Masking And Normalization
source.authors: Filip Sondej; Yu-Shi Yang; Mikolaj Kniejski; Marcel Windys

record.tranche_reason: The study reports experiments on unlearning and supervised relearning of coding ability, biohazardous knowledge, and a harmful tendency. It does not test the listed claims about safety-trained chat models’ refusal behavior, response-position KL, or bypassing refusal openings.
record.gate_note: The paper cites claims about safety fine-tuning and jailbreaks, but those cited results are not this study’s results. Its own biohazardous-knowledge relearning results are related to recovery of unwanted capabilities, but measure forget-set loss and WMDP accuracy rather than harmful-request refusal or compliance. Python and cruelty results are not included because they are less directly related to the claim’s subject.
record.test_reason: The study builds and compares unlearning methods (MUDMAN vs adapted TAR and ablations) on small pretrained models. It measures forget-set loss and WMDP-Bio accuracy after supervised relearning. It never measures harmful-request compliance or refusal in safety-trained chat models, per-token KL, prefill or suffix bypass, safety localization, or deepened safety alignment. Qi et al. (2310.03693) appears only as a citation in the introduction.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim MUDMAN outperforms TAR by about 40%. They say each component significantly improves robustness, though the figures show meta-learning and normalization do not help in every setup. They argue selective, non-disruptive unlearning moves toward irreversible removal of dangerous knowledge.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates robust unlearning followed by supervised relearning, not fine-tuning a safety-aligned model to elicit harmful requests or measuring refusal behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on the unlearning task and method; the authors say meta-learning and gradient normalization do not help in every setup. Hyperparameter choice is also emphasized as important.

fits_no_version.finding: Disruption Masking, meta-learning and gradient normalization make unlearned Pile-Bio knowledge and Python skill harder to recover with SGD relearning than adapted TAR. The comparison uses forget loss and WMDP-Bio accuracy against a no-unlearning baseline (45.5% WMDP).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sign-agreement masking of unlearning gradients improves the robustness of unlearning against supervised relearning.

fits_no_version.finding: On SmolLM-135M, unlearning cruelty with BeaverTails animal-abuse examples was only partly robust to relearning. Meta-learning did not help, and the authors speculate cruel tendencies are more 'shallow' than knowledge (Figure 6, Appendix D). No rows were recorded for this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearned harmful tendencies are recovered by relearning differently from unlearned knowledge.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 Workshop: AI That Keeps Up: Workshop on Continual and Compatible Foundation Model Updates (CCFM)
record.problems: The study evaluates supervised fine-tuning as its elicitation method and does not evaluate other attacks such as jailbreak prompts. The relevant plotted values are not numerically stated in the text. The authors note that smaller models had near-random WMDP-Bio accuracy, so the WMDP experiment is shown only for Llama-3.2-1B.
record.rows_left_out: Python unlearning and the cruelty-tendency experiments (Figures 3 and 6, and Appendix D) were omitted because they are less directly about recovery of dangerous knowledge. Appendix B module comparisons and Appendix C normalization comparisons concern unlearning performance on other settings, not the listed refusal, token-depth, or bypass claims.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning of safety-trained models to induce harmful compliance. Relearning here recovers unlearned knowledge, measured by loss or WMDP, not refusal.
Benign fine-tuning effects on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Prefilling, suffixes or decoding attacks. The authors list jailbreaks as future work.
Localization of safety in few weights. The module-selection results concern unlearning targets, not safety behaviour.
The cause of shallow safety alignment.
Training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens.

record.verdict_notes: 'discusses' vs 'cites_only' is borderline. The paper cites Qi et al. and frames safety fine-tuning as hiding rather than removing knowledge, but runs no experiment on safety-trained models. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Whether harmful fine-tuning data makes safety-trained chat models comply with harmful requests.
Whether ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning data raises harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Whether compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes defeat refusal.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether the data or training objective causes safety behavior to be shallow.
Whether training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens deepens safety and whether it remains robust.

relation.reason: The introduction discusses safety fine-tuning hiding dangerous knowledge and its recovery through jailbreaks or fine-tuning, citing prior work. The experiments evaluate robust unlearning rather than safety-aligned harmful compliance or refusal.

tranche.reason: The results compare unlearning methods using forget-set loss and hazardous-knowledge accuracy after relearning. They do not test any listed version of shallow safety alignment or use that finding as an experimental tool.

source_check.notes: All listed rows report method performance, not evidence for a claim version; their none links and cannot_determine states are appropriate. TAR is adapted by removing initial representation noising; Figure 3 uses an adversary-decay variant later omitted from the final algorithm.
